scenes.text: Most teams run software that has no API. AnyBridge lets an AI assistant operate that software anyway, with evidence, approval, and replay.
The model sees a numbered menu. It proposes a typed plan. A human approves out of band. The engine executes, verifies against the file system, and saves a hash-pinned workflow.
Here is fixture app A. The model inspects the page and returns a plan using only menu IDs. No selectors, no hard-coded URLs, and the model cannot approve its own plan.
In a separate terminal, a human runs anybridge approve, sees the plan hash, and types yes. The plan is single use and expires in ten minutes.
After execution, verification reads the data file, not the UI. The task passed because the JSON evidence says so. Then we save the workflow and replay it after a reset. Zero model calls.
Eight measured tasks passed plan, execute, verify, and replay. Compile took six seconds total. Replay took four. The engine blocked every covered attack.
Compile once, replay forever. AnyBridge is model-agnostic, MIT licensed, and ready for your own tools. Get it at the repository below.
